assumptions: §6's REGISTRY GIVES BATCH 090 THREE WORDS -- "policy/request/event" -- AND §5's INVENTORY GIVES `approval.core` THE SAME THREE OBJECTS. §4.7 of docs/plans/core-database-and-rls-workstream-th.md heads its first bullet "approval_policies / approval_policy_steps" and names a FOURTH table that no registry row in §6's 000-180 range gives to anybody and that §5 does not list. This batch creates THREE and records the fourth as a blocker rather than a deferral, on the rule batch 021 established and 060 and 080 applied: creating a table no registry row gives you is reserving somebody else's work. The difference from 080's refusal is stated rather than copied -- content_targets went to a NAMED later batch (081) and approval_policy_steps goes nowhere, because 091 is calendar/schedule.

§4.7 AND §5 DISAGREE ABOUT THE POLICY'S SCOPE AND §2 DECIDES IT, NOT THIS BATCH. §4.7: "Policy อยู่ Workspace หรือ Business scope" (nullable business). §5: Scope "business/page" (mandatory business, nullable page override). §2 of the sprint-0a document ranks itself above core-database-and-rls-workstream-th.md, which it lists as item 5, "workstream เดิม". So §5 wins, `business_profile_id` is NOT NULL, and A WORKSPACE-WIDE APPROVAL POLICY IS NOW INEXPRESSIBLE. Both sentences are quoted in the open blocker so the owner can overrule it with a forward migration rather than an edit here.

§4.7 IS STILL THE SOURCE WHERE THE WINNING DOCUMENT IS SILENT. §2's rule is about CONFLICT. The sprint-0a document supplies no approval status vocabulary, no "minimum approvers" field and no idempotency rule, so §4.7 is the only source for those and they are taken from it -- which is exactly how batch 080 took §4.6's six vocabularies from the same workstream file.

§4.7's FIVE STATUS VALUES ARE A QUOTATION AND NOT A DECISION. "status(pending|approved|changes_requested|cancelled|expired)" -- five, given -- so the CHECK carries five and a static rule asserts the set equals the document's. No sixth value is invented and no fifth is dropped.

`approval_events.action` GETS NO CHECK. §4.7 names it and enumerates nothing; §8.3's "Approve/reject/request changes" is a matrix row about who may act, not an alphabet of strings. A CHECK derived from a matrix row would be this batch choosing the event vocabulary for Product.

§8.3's TWO `P` CELLS ON THE DECIDE ROW ARE REFUSED RATHER THAN IMPLEMENTED. Admin and editor are `P` -- "ผ่านตาม policy/explicit capability" -- and no capability is defined anywhere in this repository. `approval_policies.required_role` is created with §7's five role values and is read by NO policy predicate, because nothing states what reading it would mean. Batch 070 refused the approver's `P` on "Suggestion save/dismiss/use" on the same ground.

§8.3 HAS NO SELECT ROW FOR THIS FAMILY AND THE CLIENT READ IS THEREFORE A READING. It rests on three sentences rather than one cell: §8.3's own decide row is `Y` for the approver and an approver who cannot read a request cannot approve one; §5 classes the family CONTENT-2/AUTH-3 and §9.1 gives CONTENT-2 the projection "through RLS"; and §8.4's tenant audit row spells the approver's cell "approval trail" in words where every other cell in §8 is a letter. AUTH-3's own projection is "minimum role projection" and this batch implements none, because that object is a security_invoker view with a registry row and RFC-2026-021 §8.1's read-allowlist.json does not exist. Recorded as a reading in the migration header, the CI comment, the coverage note and the blockers.

app_worker IS GRANTED NOTHING ON ALL THREE TABLES, which is batch 080's shape rather than batch 070's, and this batch has a second reason for it: §8.3 marks the Service column `P` on three rows and `N` on the fourth, so there is no `S` cell anywhere in this family for a worker grant to anticipate. Consequence: every service case is a PRIVILEGE refusal, none carries RFC-2026-017 §7, none is in the CI negative control's basis, and db/foundation/lint/service-policy-map.json gets no entry -- with a prose note saying so, which is the convention batches 110 and 132 established.

known_limitations: NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN WRITE AN APPROVAL EVENT, AND THAT IS WORSE THAN BATCH 080's EQUIVALENT RATHER THAN THE SAME. §8.3 row 4 is `N` for every role including the service, implemented as absent grants and absent policies; INSERT is absent too, on a reading rather than a quotation, because a decision trail a client can author proves nothing about the decision and the writer §8.3 points to is a SECURITY DEFINER command function owned by app_command that does not exist (RFC-2026-017 §3; RFC-2026-021 §10). A client CAN raise, cancel and decide a request through the policies this batch writes. So a decision can be taken and not recorded, and §4 invariant 8's immutable approval history stays empty while it happens.

`expired` IS IN THE VOCABULARY AND IS WRITTEN BY NOBODY. §8.3 has no row that produces it, the Service column on the three write rows is `P` with no capability, and no document states how long a request stays open. The migration FAILS AT APPLY TIME if any policy's WITH CHECK half mentions the value. A request that should expire cannot.

NOTHING KEEPS `approval_requests.status` IN STEP WITH `content_items.approval_state`. Batch 080 created that column with no CHECK and said the vocabulary belonged to a table batch 090 owns; this batch owns it now and writes no relationship between them. A request reading `approved` beside an item whose approval_state says otherwise is a disagreement no query can detect as wrong.

BATCH 160 HAS NO PATH TO §10's APPROVAL-HISTORY ANONYMISATION. app.approval_events carries `actor` and `comment` -- the two columns an anonymiser would rewrite -- and no UPDATE or DELETE grant to any role including app_maintenance, because §8.3 row 4 is `N` in every column. Recorded by the batch that caused it rather than left for 160 to discover after the migration merged.

TWO REVERSALS WENT UNNOTICED BEFORE A RULE WAS ADDED. The three new negative-control entries bit: 14, 17 and 3 cases noticed, the three on the trail being its reads alone, exactly as the ci.yml comment said in advance.

WHAT CI's GREEN DOES NOT RETIRE, AND IT IS THE LARGER HALF OF THE `do $$` BLOCK. The block ran and raised nothing, which proves its queries execute -- and an assertion that never fires is indistinguishable from one whose predicate can never be true. The nineteen probes defeated STATIC rules; none defeated an apply-time one, because that needs a mutated migration pushed to CI. The `expired` assertion and the conkey degree check are the two most worth defeating, since both are shapes no earlier batch wrote. Owed to the independent Tester.

WHETHER THE READ SURFACE IS THE RIGHT WIDTH IS NOT A QUESTION ANY TEST ANSWERS. §8.3 has no SELECT row for this family, and a viewer reads the decision trail including `approval_events.comment`. CI proves the boundary holds BETWEEN tenants; it says nothing about whether the boundary is in the right place INSIDE one.
